raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Description

Regarding: EAGLE/MTP prefix caching on hybrid (attention + Mamba) models

When serving GLM-5.3-Flash with MTP in P/D on B300s, I noticed every warm turn missed one more cached block than the same deployment with speculation off. With a fixed 77K-token shared prefix, MTP hits exactly 73,728 tokens (32 blocks) every time while spec off hits 76,032 (33 blocks), so each turn recomputes ~2.3K extra prompt tokens, about 60% more prefill work, which is what saturates prefill and drives TTFT up under load

I find that the main cause is the EAGLE trailing-block drop. It exists so a request never reuses the draft-layer KV slot at a producer's chunk end, since that slot was written with the producer's lookahead token. With one MTP head (or EAGLE) that is a single slot, and a stale one can only lower acceptance, since target verification keeps outputs exact. For regular attention the drop costs one ordinary block, but in Mamba `align` mode the attention block is sized to hold a Mamba state page (2304 tokens on GLM-5.3-Flash), so the drop recomputes a whole block on every prefix hit

This makes `disable_eagle_block_drop` default to auto (`bool | None = None`) and resolves it in `VllmConfig` right after the hybrid config hooks, so the scheduler, workers and KV connectors all read the same value:
```text
disable = method in {eagle, eagle3, mtp}
          and is_hybrid and enable_prefix_caching and mamba_cache_mode == "align"
          and num_prefill_lookahead_tokens == 1
```
an explicit setting still wins, and multi-module MTP (several lookahead slots per chunk boundary), DFlash/DSpark and non-hybrid models keep the drop

I tested this on GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 with MTP7 in 1P/1D NIXL (prefill DEP TP4×DP2/EP8, decode 2× TP4, NVFP4 KV, 1M context, 16 B300s) using native AgentX (`semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126`, 900 s per point, one run each), comparing the current drop against `disable_eagle_block_drop=true` on our internal fork, which carries the same drop logic:

| C | TTFT p50 drop → keep | out tok/s drop → keep | prefill prefix hit drop → keep | draft acceptance drop → keep |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 500 → 517 ms | 1,293 → 1,303 | 0.876 → 0.892 | 0.409 → 0.417 |
| 128 | 723 → 639 ms | 3,402 → 3,398 | 0.842 → 0.859 | 0.385 → 0.379 |
| 256 | 1,097 → 946 ms | 5,366 → 5,427 | 0.841 → 0.858 | 0.398 → 0.398 |
| 384 | 6,576 → 2,544 ms | 6,487 → 6,896 | 0.803 → 0.826 | 0.395 → 0.391 |

acceptance doesn't move, and the gain shows up once prefill becomes the bottleneck (C64/C128 are within single-run noise). Correctness gates, including ~990K-token retrieval, tool calls and streaming, passed with the block kept. I also tried `--prefix-match-unit` below the block size, which shrinks the drop to one hash unit, but mid-block hits copy a whole block per KV group on this model and were slower overall, so it isn't a substitute today

files.patch:
@@ -447,11 +447,18 @@ class SpeculativeConfig:
     speculative input batches can contain sequences of different lengths,
     which may only be supported by certain attention backends. This currently
     only affects the EAGLE method of speculation."""
-    disable_eagle_block_drop: bool = False
+    disable_eagle_block_drop: bool | None = None
     """Disable dropping the trailing prefix-cache block for EAGLE-like
-    speculative methods. This is an experimental option for measuring the
-    acceptance-rate impact of reusing that block. It does not disable the
-    speculative drafter itself."""
+    speculative methods. Reusing that block can only lower acceptance: the
+    draft KV at its last slot may encode a lookahead token that differs from
+    the new request's, but target verification keeps outputs exact. It does
+    not disable the speculative drafter itself.
+
+    If `None`, the drop is kept except for hybrid (attention + Mamba) models in
+    Mamba "align" prefix-caching mode with a single-token drafter lookahead:
+    there the block is sized to hold a Mamba state (often thousands of tokens),
+    so the drop recomputes a whole block on every prefix hit to protect one
+    draft KV slot."""
     use_local_argmax_reduction: bool = False
     """Use vocab-parallel local argmax instead of all-gathering full logits
     for draft token generation. Reduces communication from O(vocab_size) to
@@ -1910,6 +1917,26 @@ def use_eagle_block_drop(self) -> bool:
         """Whether volatile trailing cache blocks should be discarded."""
         return self.use_eagle() and not self.disable_eagle_block_drop
 
+    def resolve_eagle_block_drop(
+        self, *, hybrid_align_prefix_caching: bool, prefill_lookahead_tokens: int
+    ) -> None:
+        """Resolve an unset `disable_eagle_block_drop` (see its docstring)."""
+        if self.disable_eagle_block_drop is not None:
+            return
+        self.disable_eagle_block_drop = (
+            self.method in ("eagle", "eagle3", "mtp")
+            and hybrid_align_prefix_caching
+            and prefill_lookahead_tokens == 1
+        )
+        if self.disable_eagle_block_drop:
+            logger.info(
+                "Keeping the trailing prefix-cache block for %s on a hybrid "
+                "model: its block holds a Mamba state, so dropping it would "
+                "recompute a whole block per prefix hit. Set "
+                "disable_eagle_block_drop=False to restore the drop.",
+                self.method,
+            )
+
     def use_dflash(self) -> bool:
         return self.method == "dflash"

@@ -2723,6 +2723,16 @@ def try_verify_and_update_config(self):
         if self.model_config.is_hybrid:
             HybridAttentionMambaModelConfig.verify_and_update_config(self)
 
+        if self.speculative_config is not None:
+            self.speculative_config.resolve_eagle_block_drop(
+                hybrid_align_prefix_caching=(
+                    self.model_config.is_hybrid
+                    and self.cache_config.enable_prefix_caching
+                    and self.cache_config.mamba_cache_mode == "align"
+                ),
+                prefill_lookahead_tokens=self.num_prefill_lookahead_tokens,
+            )
+
         if self.model_config.convert_type == "classify":
             # Maybe convert ForCausalLM into ForSequenceClassification model.
             from vllm.model_executor.models.adapters import SequenceClassificationConfig
